source_refs.note: 2- Population Growth: a main subheading of Demography: Characteristics of Populations, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 236-236.

blocks.text: The Increase in the number of individuals within over a specific time period is called population growth. It is an important attribute of populations. There are two population growth models.

Exponential growth model: According to this model, the population grows without limits at its maximal rate. Rather than increasing by adding a constant number of individuals to the population in every generation, the population increases by the same ratio per unit time. Not all populations display exponential growth.

Logistic growth model: In this model, the growing population eventually reaches a limit due to shortage of resources like space, light, water, or nutrients. Such population stabilizes at a certain size, called the carrying capacity of the particular place where it lives. In these situations, growth curves assume a sigmoid, or flattened S, shape.

blocks.alt: One graph of population size (0 to 1250) against number of generations (0 to 15). Two curves start together near generation 4. Exponential growth (pink, J shape) climbs ever faster past 1000 by about generation 8.5. Logistic growth (blue, S shape) slows and levels off at the carrying capacity, about 750.
